kicker: Jev and Kimi K3, one gate

scenes.headline: How a confidence gate splits fraud checks between two models
scenes.sub: Jev decides fast; Kimi K3 re-reads the uncertain ones.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Samba! This demo sorts fraud emails with two models and a threshold between them. Here's how the gate works, and how to read its score.

scenes.text: A cheap, fast model decides every email. Only when its confidence falls below 95% does an expensive model re-read it.
scenes.say: The idea: a cheap, fast model decides every email. Only when its confidence falls below ninety-five percent does an expensive model re-read it.

steps.say: A hundred emails from a public fraud corpus go to Jev, a small, fast classifier. Each answer comes with a confidence.
A gate reads that confidence. At ninety-five percent or more, Jev's answer stands. That settled about two thirds of them.
Below it, the email goes to Kimi K3, a far larger model. Thirty-one reviews overturned five decisions. The bill leaves room for about five output tokens each: a label.

steps.note: confidence measures how peaked the answer is, not how likely it is right
steps.say: One subtlety: the confidence measures how peaked Jev's answer is, not the chance it's right. Nothing published maps one to the other.

scenes.title: Accuracy against the labels
scenes.note: Kimi K3 saw 32.3% of the volume and took 95.8% of the bill
scenes.say: The gate lifted accuracy from eighty-nine point nine to ninety-five point nine percent. The big model saw a third of the emails, and took nearly all the bill.

scenes.label: the false-positive rate that zero false alarms in 50 legitimate emails cannot rule out
scenes.note: at 0.5% prevalence, that bound puts precision at 7.4%
scenes.say: The catch: the sample was half fraud, and no inbox is. Zero false alarms in fifty can't rule out a rate up to five point eight percent.

scenes.text: A cheap model in front, an expensive one behind, a threshold deciding who pays. Judge it at a real base rate.

recap: Jev decides; below 95% confidence, Kimi K3 re-reads
Precision needs a realistic base rate to mean anything
scenes.say: To recap: a fast model decides, a threshold escalates the unsure ones, and the score only means something at a real base rate.
